@graph.articleBody: Google bills you when someone clicks your ad. It does not ask whether that person wanted to hire you, apply for a job, fix the problem themselves or buy a part. If your ad shows for a search that has nothing to do with your business, you can still pay for the click. Negative keywords are the tool that closes that gap. mainEntity.name: What is a negative keyword in Google Ads?

acceptedAnswer.text: It is a word or phrase that keeps your ad from showing for searches that contain it. Google describes negative keywords as a way to exclude search terms from your campaigns.

mainEntity.name: How do I find negative keywords for my business?

acceptedAnswer.text: Open the search terms report in your Google Ads account and read the real searches that triggered your ads. Any search that is about a job, a service you do not offer or a place you do not serve points to a word worth blocking.

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between broad, phrase and exact match for negative keywords?

acceptedAnswer.text: Broad blocks a search that contains all your negative terms in any order. Phrase blocks a search that contains the terms in the same order, even with other words around them. Exact blocks a search that contains the terms in the same order without extra words, so it is the narrowest.

mainEntity.name: Will negative keywords lower my cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: They stop your ads from showing for searches you have decided are not worth a click, but no source gives a number for how much that changes your spend. Treat them as a way to keep the budget for relevant searches, not as a savings promise.
